# ntfy-mac CLI reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-cli-docs.swift from `ntfy-mac schema --json`. Do not edit; run `make docs`. -->

Native ntfy notifications for macOS.

Every command takes --json for machine-readable output on stdout.

## Conventions

- **Output:** with `--json`, stdout carries JSON and nothing else: one document per command, one per line (NDJSON) for `tail`. Without it, stdout carries text for people.
- **Diagnostics:** progress, hints and warnings go to stderr, in both modes.
- **Errors:** with `--json` a failure prints `{"error":{"code":"...","exitCode":N,"message":"..."}}` on stdout and `Error: <message>` on stderr. The exit code is the one in the tables below.
- **Strict flags:** an unknown flag or a bad value exits 2 and does nothing.
- **Machine-readable form of this page:** `ntfy-mac schema --json`.
- **Settings:** every setting the app exposes, and the command that sets it, is in [Settings](settings.md).

## Exit codes

| Code | Name | Meaning |
|-|-|-|
| 0 | success | The command did what it was asked. |
| 1 | runtime | A runtime failure; the error code says which (see errorCodes). |
| 2 | usage | Invalid flags, arguments or values; nothing was done. |
| 3 | auth | The server rejected the token. |
| 4 | appUnavailable | The app is not running, or a system permission it needs is missing. |
| 7 | serverUnreachable | The ntfy server could not be reached. |

## Error codes

| Code | Exit | Meaning |
|-|-|-|
| usage | 2 | Invalid flags, arguments or values. |
| not-configured | 1 | No server URL or token yet; run setup. |
| config-invalid | 1 | The configured URL or token is unusable. |
| not-found | 1 | No such message in the history. |
| timeout | 1 | wait found no matching message in time. |
| unauthorized | 3 | The server rejected the token (401/403). |
| server-unreachable | 7 | The server did not answer. |
| rate-limited | 1 | The server answered 429; retry later. |
| redirected | 1 | The server redirected; the URL is wrong. |
| insecure-server | 1 | A token over plain http is refused. |
| invalid-topic | 2 | A topic name the server would not accept. |
| app-unavailable | 4 | The app is not running or not reachable. |
| permission-denied | 4 | Notifications are not allowed. |
| invalid-response | 1 | An answer that could not be read. |
| app-outdated | 1 | The running app is older than the CLI and does not know the command. |
| storage | 1 | Reading or writing local state failed. |
| internal | 1 | The app failed while handling the request. |
| topic-not-local | 1 | Only local topics can be removed. |
| no-match | 1 | No sound matches the filter. |
| cancelled | 1 | The user declined the confirmation. |
| setup-cancelled | 1 | The setup wizard was cancelled. |
| logs-failed | 1 | The log tool failed. |
| update-unsupported | 1 | This install cannot update itself. |
| update-disabled | 1 | Self-update is turned off by NTFY_MAC_NO_SELF_UPDATE=1. |
| update-not-writable | 1 | The folder that holds NtfyMac.app is not writable. |
| update-invalid | 1 | The downloaded release failed verification; nothing was installed. |
| checksum-mismatch | 1 | The download does not match the release's SHA256SUMS; nothing was installed. |
| update-failed | 1 | The upgrade failed. |
| error | 1 | Any other failure. |

## UI actions and their CLI equivalents

Everything the History window does to a message has a command. A test fails when an action has no command here.

| Action in the window | Command | Example | Notes |
|-|-|-|-|
| Acknowledge | `ntfy-mac ack` | `ntfy-mac ack alerts m1` | `--all --topic <topic>` acknowledges a whole topic. |
| Mark read | `ntfy-mac read` | `ntfy-mac read alerts m1 --json` | Reading a message marks it read; `--no-mark` leaves it. Mark unread and mark all read have no command; `ack --all --topic <topic>` also marks a topic read, and acknowledges it. |
| Remind me | `ntfy-mac remind` | `ntfy-mac remind alerts m1 --in 1h` | The window offers 15 minutes, 1 hour and tomorrow 08:00; `--until` takes any time. |
| Delete | `ntfy-mac delete` | `ntfy-mac delete alerts m1` | `--topic <topic> --all` deletes every message of a topic. |
| Open click URL | `ntfy-mac read` | `ntfy-mac read alerts m1 --no-mark --json` | Read only: the URL is the `click` field. The window opens http, https and mailto links only. |
| Export (JSON or CSV) | `ntfy-mac ls` | `ntfy-mac ls --json --topic alerts --limit 1000` | The window's JSON export has the same fields as `ls --json`. |
| Search and filter | `ntfy-mac search` | `ntfy-mac search deploy --topic builds --min-priority 4 --since 7d` | Topic, minimum priority, date and unread filters; `ls` takes the same without text. |

## `ntfy-mac setup`

Connect ntfy-mac to your ntfy server.

```
ntfy-mac setup [--url <url>] [--token <string>]
```

Without options, an interactive wizard asks for the URL and token (terminal only).

| Argument | Kind | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| `--url` | option | url |  | no | The ntfy server URL. |
| `--token` | option | string |  | no | An access token for the server. |
| `--json` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Print machine-readable JSON on stdout instead of text. |

**Needs**

- Does not use the app.
- Talks to the ntfy server with the configured URL and token.
- Reads or writes the local config or history files.

**Error codes:** `usage`, `config-invalid`, `insecure-server`, `invalid-response`, `not-configured`, `rate-limited`, `redirected`, `server-unreachable`, `setup-cancelled`, `unauthorized`. See [Error codes](#error-codes).

**Examples**

```sh
ntfy-mac setup
ntfy-mac setup --url https://ntfy.example.com --token tk_...
```

## `ntfy-mac doctor`

Check configuration, server, app and permissions.

```
ntfy-mac doctor [--send-test]
```

Read-only: it never changes the install and posts nothing unless --send-test is given. The exit code is non-zero when a check fails (3 auth, 4 app or permission, 7 server).

| Argument | Kind | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| `--send-test` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Also post a test notification through the app. |
| `--json` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Print machine-readable JSON on stdout instead of text. |

**Needs**

- Asks the app when it is running; never starts it.
- Talks to the ntfy server with the configured URL and token.
- Reads or writes the local config or history files.

**Error codes:** `usage`, `config-invalid`, `insecure-server`, `invalid-response`, `not-configured`, `rate-limited`, `redirected`, `server-unreachable`, `unauthorized`. See [Error codes](#error-codes).

**Examples**

```sh
ntfy-mac doctor
ntfy-mac doctor --json
ntfy-mac doctor --send-test
```

## `ntfy-mac subscribe`

Show the subscribed topics, add a local one, or reset.

```
ntfy-mac subscribe [<topic>]
```

subscribe <topic> adds a topic; subscribe reset clears the local additions.

| Argument | Kind | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| `topic` | positional | string |  | no | A topic to add, or `reset`. |
| `--json` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Print machine-readable JSON on stdout instead of text. |

**Needs**

- Does not use the app.
- Talks to the ntfy server with the configured URL and token.
- Reads or writes the local config or history files.

**Error codes:** `usage`, `config-invalid`, `insecure-server`, `invalid-response`, `not-configured`, `rate-limited`, `redirected`, `server-unreachable`, `unauthorized`. See [Error codes](#error-codes).

**Examples**

```sh
ntfy-mac subscribe
ntfy-mac subscribe builds
ntfy-mac subscribe reset
```

## `ntfy-mac config`

Show and change notification settings.

```
ntfy-mac config
```

| Argument | Kind | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| `--json` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Print machine-readable JSON on stdout instead of text. |

**Needs**

- Does not use the app.
- Reads or writes the local config or history files.

**Error codes:** `usage`. See [Error codes](#error-codes).

**Examples**

```sh
ntfy-mac config
ntfy-mac config show --json
ntfy-mac config sounds list
ntfy-mac config sounds set 5 Sosumi
ntfy-mac config dismiss set 3 15
ntfy-mac config dismiss set 5 never
ntfy-mac config sounds reset
ntfy-mac config get reAlert
ntfy-mac config set reAlertIntervalSeconds 600
ntfy-mac config reset reAlertIntervalSeconds
ntfy-mac config topic list
ntfy-mac config topic set builds --mute --min-priority 4 --emoji 🔨
ntfy-mac config topic show builds
ntfy-mac config topic reset builds
ntfy-mac config quiet-hours show
ntfy-mac config quiet-hours set --start 22:00 --end 07:00 --no-digest
ntfy-mac config quiet-hours off
```

### `ntfy-mac config get`

```

```

Example: ntfy-mac config get reAlertIntervalSeconds

| Argument | Kind | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| `key` | positional | `allowInsecure`, `allowPrivateNetworkActions`, `reAlert`, `reAlertIntervalSeconds`, `reAlertMaxRepeats`, `reAlertMinPriority` |  | yes | The setting. |
| `--json` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Print machine-readable JSON on stdout instead of text. |

### `ntfy-mac config set`

Change a setting.

```
ntfy-mac config set <allowInsecure|allowPrivateNetworkActions|reAlert|reAlertIntervalSeconds|reAlertMaxRepeats|reAlertMinPriority> <value>
```

Booleans take true, false, on or off. reAlertIntervalSeconds is above 0, reAlertMinPriority 1 to 5, reAlertMaxRepeats 0 or more. The running app picks the change up through its config watcher.

```sh
ntfy-mac config set reAlert off
ntfy-mac config set reAlertIntervalSeconds 600
```

| Argument | Kind | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| `key` | positional | `allowInsecure`, `allowPrivateNetworkActions`, `reAlert`, `reAlertIntervalSeconds`, `reAlertMaxRepeats`, `reAlertMinPriority` |  | yes | The setting. |
| `value` | positional | string |  | yes | The new value. |
| `--json` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Print machine-readable JSON on stdout instead of text. |

### `ntfy-mac config topic`

Show and change the settings of one topic.

```
ntfy-mac config topic
```

The topic follows the verb: ntfy-mac config topic show|set|reset <topic>. `config topic list` shows every topic with settings of its own. A muted topic is stored in the history and never notified; a minimum priority holds back messages below it.

| Argument | Kind | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| `--json` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Print machine-readable JSON on stdout instead of text. |

```
ntfy-mac config topic list

|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| `--json` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Print machine-readable JSON on stdout instead of text. |

```

#### `ntfy-mac config topic set`

Mute a topic, filter it by priority, or give it an emoji.

```
ntfy-mac config topic set <topic> [--mute] [--unmute] [--min-priority <integer>] [--emoji <string>]
```

At least one option is required. --min-priority takes 1 to 5, or none to remove the filter; --emoji takes an emoji for the notification title, or none to remove it.

```sh
ntfy-mac config topic set builds --mute
ntfy-mac config topic set builds --min-priority 4 --emoji 🔨
```

| Argument | Kind | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| `topic` | positional | string |  | yes | The topic. |
| `--mute` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Store messages without notifying. |
| `--unmute` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Notify again. |
| `--min-priority` | option | integer (1 to 5) |  | no | Hold back messages below this priority (1-5), or none. |
| `--emoji` | option | string |  | no | Prefix for the notification title, or none. |
| `--json` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Print machine-readable JSON on stdout instead of text. |

#### `ntfy-mac config topic reset`

```
ntfy-mac config topic reset <topic>
```

| Argument | Kind | Type | Default | Required | Description |

### `ntfy-mac config quiet-hours`

Hold notifications back during a daily window.

```
ntfy-mac config quiet-hours
```

Messages that arrive inside the window are stored and not notified. Priority 5 can bypass the window, and a digest can summarise what was held when the window ends.

| Argument | Kind | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| `--json` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Print machine-readable JSON on stdout instead of text. |

#### `ntfy-mac config quiet-hours show`

Show the quiet-hours schedule.

```
ntfy-mac config quiet-hours show
```

| Argument | Kind | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| `--json` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Print machine-readable JSON on stdout instead of text. |

#### `ntfy-mac config quiet-hours set`

Change the quiet-hours schedule and turn it on.

```
ntfy-mac config quiet-hours set [--start <time>] [--end <time>] [--urgent-bypass] [--no-urgent-bypass] [--digest] [--no-digest]
```

Times are local, HH:mm (24 hours). The window may cross midnight. Options you leave out keep their value; the defaults are 22:00 to 07:00 with urgent bypass and digest on.

```sh
ntfy-mac config quiet-hours set --start 22:00 --end 07:00
ntfy-mac config quiet-hours set --no-urgent-bypass --no-digest
```

| Argument | Kind | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| `--start` | option | time (HH:mm) |  | no | Start of the window, HH:mm. |
| `--end` | option | time (HH:mm) |  | no | End of the window, HH:mm (exclusive). |
| `--urgent-bypass` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Let priority 5 through. |
| `--no-urgent-bypass` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Hold priority 5 back too. |
| `--digest` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Summarise what was held when the window ends. |
| `--no-digest` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Show what was held one by one when the window ends. |
| `--json` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Print machine-readable JSON on stdout instead of text. |

#### `ntfy-mac config quiet-hours off`

Turn quiet hours off and keep the times.

```
ntfy-mac config quiet-hours off
```

| Argument | Kind | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| `--json` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Print machine-readable JSON on stdout instead of text. |

## `ntfy-mac notify`

Send a local notification through the app (no server needed).

```
ntfy-mac notify [--message <string>] [--title <string>] [--priority <integer>] [--tag <string>...] [--url <url>] [--dismiss-after <number>]
```

With --json the payload is read from stdin and the result is printed as JSON:

```sh
echo '{"title":"T","body":"B"}' | ntfy-mac notify --json
```

| Argument | Kind | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| `--message`, `-m` | option | string |  | no | The notification text. |
| `--title`, `-t` | option | string |  | no | The title (default: ntfy-mac). |
| `--priority`, `-p` | option | integer (1 to 5) |  | no | Priority 1-5 (sound and urgency). |
| `--tag` | option | string |  | no | An emoji tag name; repeatable. Repeatable. |
| `--url` | option | url |  | no | Open this URL when the notification is clicked. |
| `--dismiss-after`, `-d` | option | number (seconds) |  | no | Remove the notification after this many seconds (0 keeps it). |
| `--json` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Print machine-readable JSON on stdout instead of text. |

**Needs**

- Starts the app when it is down.

**Error codes:** `usage`, `app-unavailable`, `permission-denied`. See [Error codes](#error-codes).

**Examples**

```sh
ntfy-mac notify -m "Deploy complete"
ntfy-mac notify -t Alert -m "Disk usage above 90%" -p 5
echo '{"title":"T","body":"B"}' | ntfy-mac notify --json
```

**Needs**

- Does not use the app.

**Error codes:** `usage`, `checksum-mismatch`, `server-unreachable`, `update-disabled`, `update-failed`, `update-invalid`, `update-not-writable`, `update-unsupported`. See [Error codes](#error-codes).

**Examples**

```sh
ntfy-mac update --check
ntfy-mac update
```

## `ntfy-mac uninstall`

Remove ntfy-mac's config, history, state and token.

```
ntfy-mac uninstall [--yes]
```

The app itself is not deleted; the output says how to remove it. A running app also gives up its login item.

| Argument | Kind | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| `--yes` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Do not ask for confirmation (required without a terminal). |
| `--json` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Print machine-readable JSON on stdout instead of text. |

**Needs**

- Asks the app when it is running; never starts it.
- Reads or writes the local config or history files.

**Error codes:** `usage`, `cancelled`. See [Error codes](#error-codes).

**Examples**

```sh
ntfy-mac uninstall --yes
```

## `ntfy-mac status`

Show the connection, pause, permissions and history counts.

```
ntfy-mac status [--require-running]
```

Asks the running app without starting it; if it is down, running is false and everything the files know (config, history) is still reported, with exit 0. --require-running exits 4 instead when the app is not running. With --json every key is always present.

| Argument | Kind | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| `--require-running` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Exit 4 when the app is not running. |
| `--json` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Print machine-readable JSON on stdout instead of text. |

**Needs**

- Asks the app when it is running; never starts it.
- Reads or writes the local config or history files.

**Error codes:** `usage`, `storage`. See [Error codes](#error-codes).

**Examples**

```sh
ntfy-mac status --json
ntfy-mac status --require-running
```

## `ntfy-mac ls`

List messages from the history, newest first.

```
ntfy-mac ls [--topic <string>] [--unread] [--unacked] [--min-priority <integer>] [--since <duration-or-timestamp>] [--limit <integer>]
```

Reads the history database directly; the app need not run. With --json the output is an array of message objects (topic, id, time, title, message, priority, tags, read, acknowledged, click, attachments). An empty or missing history is an empty list.

| Argument | Kind | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| `--topic` | option | string |  | no | Only this topic. |
| `--unread` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Only unread messages. |
| `--unacked` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Only messages that are not acknowledged. |
| `--min-priority` | option | integer (1 to 5) |  | no | Only messages with at least this priority (1-5). |
| `--since` | option | duration-or-timestamp |  | no | Only messages since a duration ago (30m, 2h, 1d) or an ISO 8601 time. |
| `--limit` | option | integer (1 to 1000) | `20` | no | At most this many messages (1-1000, default 20). |
| `--json` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Print machine-readable JSON on stdout instead of text. |

**Needs**

- Does not use the app.
- Reads or writes the local config or history files.

**Error codes:** `usage`, `storage`. See [Error codes](#error-codes).

**Examples**

```sh
ntfy-mac ls --json --topic alerts --unread --limit 5
ntfy-mac ls --unacked --min-priority 4 --since 2h
```

## `ntfy-mac search`

Search the history by text, newest first.

```
ntfy-mac search <query> [--topic <string>] [--unread] [--unacked] [--min-priority <integer>] [--since <duration-or-timestamp>] [--limit <integer>]
```

Full-text search over titles and messages; every word matches as a prefix. Takes the same filters and prints the same output as ls.

| Argument | Kind | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| `query` | positional | string |  | yes | The words to search for. |
| `--topic` | option | string |  | no | Only this topic. |
| `--unread` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Only unread messages. |
| `--unacked` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Only messages that are not acknowledged. |
| `--min-priority` | option | integer (1 to 5) |  | no | Only messages with at least this priority (1-5). |
| `--since` | option | duration-or-timestamp |  | no | Only messages since a duration ago (30m, 2h, 1d) or an ISO 8601 time. |
| `--limit` | option | integer (1 to 1000) | `20` | no | At most this many messages (1-1000, default 20). |
| `--json` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Print machine-readable JSON on stdout instead of text. |

**Needs**

- Does not use the app.
- Reads or writes the local config or history files.

**Error codes:** `usage`, `storage`. See [Error codes](#error-codes).

**Examples**

```sh
ntfy-mac search disk --json
ntfy-mac search deploy --topic builds --since 1d
```

## `ntfy-mac read`

Show one message in full and mark it read.

```
ntfy-mac read <topic> <id> [--no-mark]
```

Marking read writes to the history database directly (WAL with a busy timeout, safe next to the running app); --no-mark leaves the state alone. An unknown message exits 1 with the error code not-found.

| Argument | Kind | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| `topic` | positional | string |  | yes | The topic. |
| `id` | positional | string |  | yes | The message id. |
| `--no-mark` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Do not mark the message read. |
| `--json` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Print machine-readable JSON on stdout instead of text. |

**Needs**

- Does not use the app.
- Reads or writes the local config or history files.

**Error codes:** `usage`, `not-found`, `storage`. See [Error codes](#error-codes).

**Examples**

```sh
ntfy-mac read alerts m1 --json
ntfy-mac read alerts m1 --no-mark
```

## `ntfy-mac ack`

Acknowledge a message, or every unacknowledged one.

```
ntfy-mac ack [<topic>] [<id>] [--all] [--topic <string>]
```

Goes through the app (started if needed): it withdraws the notification and stops its re-alerts. ack <topic> <id> acknowledges one message and exits 1 with the error code not-found for an unknown one; ack --all [--topic T] acknowledges everything pending.

| Argument | Kind | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| `topic` | positional | string |  | no | The topic. |
| `id` | positional | string |  | no | The message id. |
| `--all` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Acknowledge every unacknowledged message. |
| `--topic` | option | string |  | no | With --all: only this topic. |
| `--json` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Print machine-readable JSON on stdout instead of text. |

**Needs**

- Starts the app when it is down.

**Error codes:** `usage`, `app-unavailable`, `internal`, `not-found`, `permission-denied`. See [Error codes](#error-codes).

**Examples**

```sh
ntfy-mac ack alerts m1
ntfy-mac ack --all --topic alerts
```

## `ntfy-mac remind`

Show a message again later.

```
ntfy-mac remind <topic> <id> [--in <duration>] [--until <timestamp>]
```

Goes through the app (started if needed): the message is shown again as a notification when the time comes (the app checks every 30 seconds). Pass --in with a duration (s, m, h and d, alone or combined: 15m, 1h, 1h30m) or --until with an ISO 8601 time in the future. An unknown message exits 1 with the error code not-found.

| Argument | Kind | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| `topic` | positional | string |  | yes | The topic. |
| `id` | positional | string |  | yes | The message id. |
| `--in` | option | duration |  | no | Remind after this long, like 15m, 1h or 1d. |
| `--until` | option | timestamp |  | no | Remind at this ISO 8601 time. |
| `--json` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Print machine-readable JSON on stdout instead of text. |

**Needs**

- Starts the app when it is down.

**Error codes:** `usage`, `app-unavailable`, `internal`, `not-found`, `permission-denied`. See [Error codes](#error-codes).

**Examples**

```sh
ntfy-mac remind alerts m1 --in 1h
ntfy-mac remind alerts m1 --until 2030-01-01T08:00:00Z
```

## `ntfy-mac delete`

Delete a message, or every message of a topic.

```
ntfy-mac delete [<topic>] [<id>] [--all] [--topic <string>]
```

Goes through the app (started if needed): the message leaves the history, its notification and re-alerts stop, and it is never shown again. delete <topic> <id> removes one message and exits 1 with the error code not-found for an unknown one; delete --topic T --all removes the whole topic. There is no undo and no prompt. An app from before this command exists answers with the error code app-outdated.

| Argument | Kind | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| `topic` | positional | string |  | no | The topic. |
| `id` | positional | string |  | no | The message id. |
| `--all` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Delete every message of --topic. |
| `--topic` | option | string |  | no | With --all: the topic to empty. |
| `--json` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Print machine-readable JSON on stdout instead of text. |

**Needs**

- Starts the app when it is down.

**Error codes:** `usage`, `app-outdated`, `app-unavailable`, `internal`, `not-found`, `permission-denied`. See [Error codes](#error-codes).

**Examples**

```sh
ntfy-mac delete alerts m1
ntfy-mac delete --topic alerts --all
```

## `ntfy-mac tail`

Print messages as NDJSON, optionally following new ones.

```
ntfy-mac tail [--topic <string>] [--unread] [--unacked] [--min-priority <integer>] [--since <duration-or-timestamp>] [--limit <integer>] [--follow]
```

One message object per line (the shape of ls --json), oldest first, whether or not --json is given. --follow keeps polling the history database every 500 ms and ends cleanly on SIGINT. Messages older than a minute when they are stored (a catch-up after an outage) are not followed.

| Argument | Kind | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| `--topic` | option | string |  | no | Only this topic. |
| `--unread` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Only unread messages. |
| `--unacked` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Only messages that are not acknowledged. |
| `--min-priority` | option | integer (1 to 5) |  | no | Only messages with at least this priority (1-5). |
| `--since` | option | duration-or-timestamp |  | no | Only messages since a duration ago (30m, 2h, 1d) or an ISO 8601 time. |
| `--limit` | option | integer (1 to 1000) | `20` | no | At most this many messages (1-1000, default 20). |
| `--follow`, `-f` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Keep running and print new messages as they arrive. |
| `--json` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Print machine-readable JSON on stdout instead of text. |

**Needs**

- Does not use the app.
- Reads or writes the local config or history files.

**Error codes:** `usage`, `storage`. See [Error codes](#error-codes).

**Examples**

```sh
ntfy-mac tail --topic alerts --since 1h --limit 10
ntfy-mac tail --topic alerts --follow
```

## `ntfy-mac wait`

Block until a matching message arrives.

```
ntfy-mac wait --topic <string> --match <string> [--timeout <number>] [--min-priority <integer>] [--ack]
```

For scripts and agents waiting on a human. Only messages that arrive after the command started count. --match is a case-insensitive substring of title or message, or /regex/ (/regex/i ignores case). Exit 0 prints the message; no match within --timeout seconds exits 1 with the error code timeout. --ack acknowledges the match through the app after it is printed.

| Argument | Kind | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| `--topic` | option | string |  | yes | The topic to watch. |
| `--match` | option | string |  | yes | A substring, or /regex/, to find in the title or message. |
| `--timeout` | option | number (seconds) | `300.0` | no | Give up after this many seconds (default 300). |
| `--min-priority` | option | integer (1 to 5) |  | no | Only messages with at least this priority (1-5). |
| `--ack` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Acknowledge the matching message. |
| `--json` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Print machine-readable JSON on stdout instead of text. |

**Needs**

- Starts the app when it is down.
- Reads or writes the local config or history files.
- Starts the app only with --ack.

**Error codes:** `usage`, `app-unavailable`, `internal`, `not-found`, `permission-denied`, `storage`, `timeout`. See [Error codes](#error-codes).

**Examples**

```sh
ntfy-mac wait --topic alerts --match approve --timeout 600 --json
ntfy-mac wait --topic alerts --match '/^approve/i' --ack
```

## `ntfy-mac publish`

Publish a message to a topic on the ntfy server.

```
ntfy-mac publish <topic> --message <string> [--title <string>] [--priority <integer>] [--tag <string>...] [--click <url>]
```

Sends the message with the configured token (never over plain http unless allowInsecure is set). -m - reads the message from stdin. Prints the id and time the server assigned.

```sh
echo "build done" | ntfy-mac publish builds -m - -t CI -p 4 --tag white_check_mark
```

| Argument | Kind | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| `topic` | positional | string |  | yes | The topic to publish to. |
| `--message`, `-m` | option | string |  | yes | The message text, or - to read stdin. |
| `--title`, `-t` | option | string |  | no | The title. |
| `--priority`, `-p` | option | integer (1 to 5) |  | no | Priority 1-5. |
| `--tag` | option | string |  | no | An emoji tag name; repeatable. Repeatable. |
| `--click` | option | url |  | no | Open this URL when the notification is clicked. |
| `--json` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Print machine-readable JSON on stdout instead of text. |

**Needs**

- Does not use the app.
- Talks to the ntfy server with the configured URL and token.
- Reads or writes the local config or history files.

**Error codes:** `usage`, `config-invalid`, `insecure-server`, `invalid-response`, `invalid-topic`, `not-configured`, `rate-limited`, `redirected`, `server-unreachable`, `unauthorized`. See [Error codes](#error-codes).

**Examples**

```sh
ntfy-mac publish builds -m "Deploy complete" -t CI -p 4
echo "build done" | ntfy-mac publish builds -m - --tag white_check_mark
```

## `ntfy-mac pause`

Hold notifications back for a while.

```
ntfy-mac pause [--for <duration>] [--until <timestamp>]
```

Writes pausedUntil to the config file; the running app picks it up through its config watcher, so it need not be reachable. Held-back messages are stored and shown when the pause ends. Without --for or --until the pause lasts until `ntfy-mac resume`. Durations use s, m, h and d, alone or combined: 30m, 2h, 1d, 1h30m.

| Argument | Kind | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| `--for` | option | duration |  | no | Pause for this long, like 30m, 2h or 1d. |
| `--until` | option | timestamp |  | no | Pause until this ISO 8601 time. |
| `--json` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Print machine-readable JSON on stdout instead of text. |

**Needs**

- Does not use the app.
- Reads or writes the local config or history files.

**Error codes:** `usage`, `storage`. See [Error codes](#error-codes).

**Examples**

```sh
ntfy-mac pause --for 30m
ntfy-mac pause --until 2030-01-01T08:00:00Z
ntfy-mac pause
```

## `ntfy-mac resume`

End a pause and show what was held back.

```
ntfy-mac resume
```

Clears pausedUntil in the config file; the running app picks it up.

| Argument | Kind | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| `--json` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Print machine-readable JSON on stdout instead of text. |

**Needs**

- Does not use the app.
- Reads or writes the local config or history files.

**Error codes:** `usage`, `storage`. See [Error codes](#error-codes).

**Examples**

```sh
ntfy-mac resume
```

The app owns its login item, so this asks the app (started if needed). States: enabled, requiresApproval (approve it in System Settings > General > Login Items), notRegistered, notFound.

| Argument | Kind | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| `action` | positional | `off`, `on`, `status` |  | yes | on, off or status. |
| `--json` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Print machine-readable JSON on stdout instead of text. |

**Needs**

- Starts the app when it is down.

**Error codes:** `usage`, `app-unavailable`, `internal`. See [Error codes](#error-codes).

**Examples**

```sh
ntfy-mac login-item status
ntfy-mac login-item on
```

## `ntfy-mac migrate`

Remove the leftovers of a 1.x install.

```
ntfy-mac migrate [--dry-run]
```

Stops and removes the 1.x LaunchAgent or brew service, the daemon, the ntfy-notify helper app and its Launch Services entries, the old binary and logs. config.json and state.json stay. The app does this itself on launch; run it by hand when doctor reports leftovers.

| Argument | Kind | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| `--dry-run` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | List what would be removed and change nothing. |
| `--json` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Print machine-readable JSON on stdout instead of text. |

**Needs**

- Does not use the app.
- Reads or writes the local config or history files.

**Error codes:** `usage`. See [Error codes](#error-codes).

**Examples**

```sh
ntfy-mac migrate --dry-run
ntfy-mac migrate
ntfy-mac migrate --json
```

## `ntfy-mac schema`

Describe every command, flag, exit code and error code.

```
ntfy-mac schema
```

With --json: one document with the full command tree (arguments with type, default, range, required, repeatable; what each command needs from the app, server and files; its error codes) plus the stable exit and error code lists. Keys are sorted, so the output is deterministic. Without --json: a compact usage listing.

| Argument | Kind | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| `--json` | flag | boolean | `false` | no | Print machine-readable JSON on stdout instead of text. |

**Needs**

- Does not use the app.

**Error codes:** `usage`. See [Error codes](#error-codes).

**Examples**

```sh
ntfy-mac schema --json
```
